face._comment: §154 — the base tone of the dial's radial-gradient face. geometry.js's DIAL_TINT_RATIO_IN/OUT hold the shipped inner/outer gradient stops as ratios to this default, so any new tone keeps the same soft vignette rather than going flat, and this default reproduces the exact literals it replaces. LIVE since §157: makeDial exposes userData.recolourFace, which repaints this canvas and every well deriving its tone from it, so APPLIERS.dial names 'face' beside 'hands' and no reload is needed. NO _bounds, and that is a decision rather than an omission (§157, roadmap item 140's second ask): _bounds is a numeric [min,max] consumed only by the panel's slider path, and a colour renders as input[type=color], which has no min or max to give it — the interval simply has no meaning here. The real constraint on this value is LEGIBILITY, which is not an interval in any case: it is a contrast floor against the fixed printed ink, and it is asserted as one (DIAL_INK_CONTRAST_MIN, WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11) at build and on every live recolour.

plate._smokeComment: §220 — THE SMOKE: `smoke` is the coat's visible TRANSMITTANCE T, 1 = the clear crystal (the shipped picture, byte for byte — materials.js asserts the identity at boot). A Lange Lumen's smoke is a thin-film coating on colourless sapphire, not a tinted crystal, and CRYSTAL_GLASS is already a coating model (a colour at an alpha, no thickness term), so the smoked dial is a second RECIPE on the same glass: light crosses the coat twice (in, off the nickel plate, out), so the plate behind contributes T², and materials.js's smokedGlass(T) folds the clear crystal's own layer and a black coat at 1 − T² into the one alpha material the renderer can blend in a single pass — opacity αc + (1 − αc)(1 − T²), colour C·αc/opacity. The plate body and the pocket walls carry it; the print sheets keep the clear crystal's layer (a sheet is print ON the coated glass, not a second coat), and the ink is solved against the composite the renderer paints — sheet over body over nickel — through makeDial's one groundAt, so the §196 solve flips to the light pole on its own as T falls (derived on that composite: dark pole down to 0.59, light from 0.58; tools/probe-220-smoke.mjs boots both and holds it) and the §157 gate holds the floor at build. RELOAD-TIER like `sapphire`, for its reason: the materials are chosen at build and the x-ray map is built over them — under x-ray a smoked material is swapped for its clear twin (a smoked plate at 0.86 would hide the works the toggle exists to show) and restored after. Inert unless `sapphire` is on; the panel disables the slider while the box is off. _bounds: the ceiling is the clear crystal; the FLOOR, 0.41, is DERIVED from the reserve sub-dial's own legibility gate, which binds before the works do. That gate holds each coloured zone's best tone to 3:1 against BOTH the face and the ticks (geometry.js, WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11); on a smoked ground the ticks go light, so the only tone with room is black, and black holds 3:1 against the face only while the ground's relative luminance is ≥ 0.10 ((Y + 0.05)/0.05 ≥ 3). The rendered composite crosses 0.10 between T 0.40 (Y 0.0997, the zone at 2.99:1 — boot WARNS) and 0.41 (Y 0.1043, 3.09:1 — silent), so 0.41 is the first slider step that boots silent; tools/probe-220-smoke.mjs boots both and holds it, and lifting this floor moves the warning, never the gate. The works themselves stay readable well below that: tools/probe-220-smoke.mjs --scan measures, on the built scene from the Dial preset, the CIELAB lightness separation ΔL* between the works and the ground they stand on in a works-only patch of the frame (blued steel — the hands and the works' screw heads — masked by colour, the masked count printed per boot) and finds where it falls to the just-noticeable difference (ΔL* 2.3, the CIE 1976 JND): T 0.27 at landing (reads at 0.27, not at 0.26) — a REPORT beside the derived floor, recorded in the §220 BUILT entry, and the reason the floor is the zones' and not the works'. SC 1.4.11's 3:1 was tried for the works first and failed its own clear-dial control at 2.56:1: the works are large shapes read at lower contrast than that small-object floor assumes. The scan lifts this floor for its own boots, since it measures what lies under it. Browser-local like every finish knob but the dial colour; it does not travel in a link. Not modelled, and said so: the luminous compound the real coating exists to charge (no lume exists in the sim), a non-neutral or graded smoke, and the second pass of the coat on specular reflections from the works behind.
plate._comment: §3 — the box sapphire dial, the half of that entry the case left unbuilt. On, the dial's MATTER becomes sapphire — the plate, its pocket walls and the sheets its print is laid on take the case crystal's own glass (materials.js CRYSTAL_GLASS, corundum's ior) — while the chapter ring, the applied numerals and the feet stay the metal they are, so the keyless works, motion works, reserve train and minute jumper read through the print from the front. RELOAD-TIER, deliberately (§22's precedent): makeDial chooses the materials at build and the x-ray map is built over them, so a live swap would be a second owner of the same slots. Geometry is untouched by construction — the same loops, the same merged body — which is what keeps the fingerprint still. The print's ink is SOLVED against the ground that actually stands behind it: the crystal's tint over the base plate's nickel (both read off the materials, never retyped), and the §157 legibility gate holds that composite the way it holds the silvered face. Not modelled, and said so: a box dial's raised rim (the plate keeps its chamfered outline), and any depth to the glass beyond the plate's own thickness. Browser-local like every finish knob but the dial colour; it does not travel in a link.

hands._comment: hour/minute carry no depth keys, deliberately (§188): the central sections are cut from HAND_STOCK_MM in geometry.js, so a depth knob here would be a lying parameter — the keys existed, were read, and had no effect on the built mesh (bossH overwrote their only consumer). The `second` kind keeps its depth keys because they are live there: counterweight thickness and that kind's boss law. widthFactor is now exactly what its label says — the plan width (halfW = length·widthFactor·0.35·√3/2) — and no longer drags thickness or boss with it. A persisted override of the removed keys is refused by the loader's type anchoring (aesthetics.js), the same rule the subdials layer's note cites.

subdials._comment: This layer holds NO sub-dial knob, deliberately. Both properties are dimensions of the SPEC: position (§94 — ?d4= moves the seconds station, ?rsvr= the reserve station) and size (§97 — ?subdialr= sets the shared well radius, held by the solver between its derived floor and TODO 33's ceiling). The radiusFactor that lived here was §23's finish knob over the solved radius; §97 retired it because a spec must be reproducible from its URL, and a browser-local multiplier on a spec dimension meant the link and the picture could disagree silently, per machine. A persisted override of the removed key is refused by the loader's type anchoring (aesthetics.js) — proven, not assumed.

gong._comment: The alarm gong's ringing wire. arcDeg is measured BACK FROM THE FREE (struck) end, so changing it moves the FOOT and leaves the hammer, its pivot and the strike point exactly where they are. Both feed the synthesised tone: f_n = (beta_n L)^2 (d/4) sqrt(E/rho) / (2 pi L^2) for a clamped-free steel bar, so the gong is heard at the pitch its dimensions imply rather than at a chosen note. Both defaults are DERIVED and main.js warns if either drifts from its derivation. §198 took the ring outside the three-quarter plate's rim, into the annulus over the base plate's mounting rim, so: wireDiaUnits is the CEILING OF REAL ALARM-GONG STOCK (1.1 mm), because the radiated power of a struck wire rises with its section and out there the room is taller than any gong wire is drawn to — the band's height is asserted, never the sizing; arcDeg is the length that puts the FUNDAMENTAL on 2.5 kHz (TODO 17's figure, the A-weighted peak of hearing) at the ring's radius, and since no plate opening exists at that radius the block lands exactly there — TODO 127 closed. A live edit walks the foot past anything on the rim by the same clear-station rule the boot applies. See TODO 17 and §198.

ribbing._comment: Glashuette stripes on the 3/4 plate + escape bridge. widthUnits = band pitch in model units, so LARGER means FEWER ribs — the default sits at the bound maximum, i.e. ribbing at its minimum (was 6.7); angleDeg = direction the bands PROGRESS in (stripes run perpendicular); tilt = normal scallop strength (0 = off). Stripes are computed from WORLD position in the shader, so they continue across separate parts by construction.

perlage._comment: Circular graining on the BASE plate, stamped like the real thing: pearls in a staggered grid, each fragment shaded by the LAST pearl (row-major application order) whose radius covers it — so every pearl overlaps its neighbours in one direction, shingled. pearlRadiusUnits > pitch/2 sets the overlap.

steel._comment: §203 step 2 — the steel's FINISH, one slider from polished (0) to brushed (1), default brushed (owner's call). It reaches MATS.steel (the works) and MATS.caseMetal (the case exterior) alike. Both ends are constraints rather than tastes: at 0 the roughness sits on the renderer's own floor (0.0525 — lights_physical_fragment clamps below it, so a smaller number does nothing) with the lobe isotropic; at 1 the lobe is fully anisotropic (the BRDF's own saturation) and the across-grain roughness is STEEL_FINISH's 0.30 — an authored number with no derivation, roadmap item 86's class, named as such in materials.js rather than laundered here. Between them both quantities mix linearly. The GRAIN DIRECTION is a world-space law in materials.js, never the UV tangent: flats (|n.z| above the ribbing's cos 45° gate) are straight-grained along brushAngleDeg in the plate plane, everything else is grained circumferentially about the movement axis (cross(z, n)) — the direction a lathe or a turning brush leaves on an arbor or a band. Live: APPLIERS.materials writes both materials, and the anisotropy define is held ON across the whole range (a floor of 1e-3 is the shader's zero) so a drag is a uniform write, never a recompile.

caseMetal._comment: §203 step 3 — the CASE EXTERIOR's metal (MATS.caseMetal: the band, back ring, sleeves and collars, both crowns, the pusher cap — step 1's split), a PICK rather than a slider: one of the `_options` keys, never a free string. It reaches the case and never the works: a spring, a pinion or a lever in gold or platinum would be a lie about the metal. Each alloy's base colour is DERIVED, not authored — a metalness-1 material's colour IS its normal-incidence reflectance F0, computed by tools/derive-203-alloys.mjs from measured optical constants (refractiveindex.info's tables, primary sources cited there) and held in materials.js ALLOY_COLORS with the derivation's two controls; steel keeps the authored 0xd6d9dd for continuity, named as underived there. 18K white gold reads as its rhodium plate. It TRAVELS as ?metal=<key> under §185's rule (a link overrides the store and never writes it) and the loader refuses any value outside `_options` — a persisted or linked key from a retired alloy is reported on the refused line, never applied. `_options` is a sibling of `_bounds` and `_labels`: the same underscore convention (schema, not a parameter), read by the panel to render a select whose option TEXT is translated and whose values stay canonical (display translates, values do not).

ruby._comment: Bearing jewels, pallet stones, impulse pin. Read at material creation and updatable live; the advanced panel writes here.
